provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The walk itself is D4-equivariant. Tip detection tries all four directions and needs a unique extreme cell plus mirror symmetry. Turns go perpendicular, to the nearest dot. Re-stamping uses (forward, sideways) local offsets. So the emitted program keeps that mechanism unchanged and runs it in visible coordinates.

The only orientation-dependent part is the panel layout. Originally the dividers are full-height columns and the start panel is the leftmost. The factory pushes the original 'left' vector (0,-1) through the transform: a horizontal flip for d4>=4, then (dy,dx)->(dx,-dy) for each clockwise turn. That tells it whether the visible dividers are full-height columns or full-width rows, and whether the first panel is at the start (left/top) or the end (right/bottom).

The program then:
- takes the grid's most common colour as background,
- finds uniform non-background divider lines along the chosen axis and crops the correct first panel (the whole grid if there are none),
- splits the panel's non-background cells into 8-connected components; the largest is the shape and every other cell is a dot,
- finds the symmetric tip, runs the eat/turn walk (nearest dot ahead, otherwise the nearer perpendicular dot), and stamps only the final shape on a background panel.

Colours are inferred from frequency and connectivity, so the palette needs no constants.
draft_notes.limitations:
- Assumes the constructor's guarantees: one multi-cell shape with exactly one symmetric tip, isolated dots never 8-adjacent to the shape or to each other, no left/right ties, and panel lines that can never be fully covered by shape or dot colour.
- On an exact left/right distance tie (which the generator excludes), it prefers the perpendicular (d[1], -d[0]) first, as the archived solver does; that choice is not D4-symmetric.
- Uneaten dots are cleared. The generator guarantees every dot is eaten, so this never matters within its domain.
- No contradictions with a uniform rule were found in the fixtures.
- Not executed by me; verification is left to the host.
